title: Late have I loved you (Confessions 10.27)
hook: beauty so ancient and so new: you were within, and I was outside
tomorrow: if no one asks you, you know. so what is time?

segments.voice: This week walked through Augustine's book: a friend's grave, an arena, a visitor's story, a garden, a window, and the palaces of memory. Yesterday's line: the fields of memory.
screen: `A GRAVE, AN ARENA, A GARDEN, A WINDOW.` → `THE FIELDS OF MEMORY.`

segments.voice: Searching the whole house for your glasses while they sit on your head. Augustine's version isn't funny to him. After all those pages of looking, he stops telling his story in the Confessions and speaks straight to God, and the first word is late. He says it twice. Late have I loved you, beauty so ancient and so new. Late have I loved you.
screen: `THE GLASSES ON YOUR HEAD.` → `LATE, SAID TWICE.` → `SO ANCIENT AND SO NEW.`

segments.voice: Then the answer to yesterday's question. You were within, and I was outside, and that's where I looked for you. I rushed at the lovely things you had made. You were with me, and I was not with you. He had searched the palaces of memory, and God was nearer than that. Then the senses take turns. You called and shouted, and broke through my deafness. You flashed and shone, and scattered my blindness. You breathed fragrance, and I drew in my breath, and now I pant for you. I tasted, and now I hunger and thirst. You touched me, and I burned for your peace. Notice he doesn't call the lovely things bad. God made them. The trouble was the order: he loved the gifts and missed the giver. And here's the thing to pass on: the whole prayer is spoken from after. Late, yes. Not too late.
screen: `YOU WERE WITHIN.` · `I WAS OUTSIDE.` · `CALLED, FLASHED, BREATHED, TOUCHED.` · `THE GIFTS, AND THE GIVER.` · then, large: `LATE HAVE I LOVED THEE.`

segments.voice: Rest one hand flat over your heart and let the other lie open in your lap. Breathe under your hand for the sit, and let Augustine's three words stay there with you: you were within. If you pray, you can rest there without any words of your own.
Late have I loved you. Augustine's cry in Book Ten: beauty so ancient and so new, found within, where he hadn't looked.
screen: `LATE HAVE I LOVED YOU — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: late have I loved thee. Late, and still in time. That's two weeks, done.

screen: `DAY 1624 COUNTS.` → `THE SAINTS IN THEIR OWN WORDS · 23 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: IF NO ONE ASKS YOU, YOU KNOW. SO WHAT IS TIME?`

howItsDone: Christians quote this passage of the Confessions in prayer and preaching, and in the Catholic Office of Readings it is read on Augustine's feast day.

match.prompt: late have I loved you — tap the pairs.

myth: Augustine calls the lovely things of the world evil
God made them. the trouble was loving the gifts and missing the giver.
in the prayer, God was within while Augustine looked outside
you were within, and I was outside, and there I looked for you.
Augustine is saying it's too late for him
the popular misreading. 'late' is said from inside the love he found.

fork.setup: your uncle started going to church in his sixties and jokes that he 'missed the good years.' what does Augustine's prayer offer him?
options: he's right: the early years were the ones that counted.
late is real, and so is love found late; God was within.
he should keep quiet about it; it's a little embarrassing.
fork.reveal: late have I loved you, Augustine says, twice. but the prayer is spoken from inside the love, not from outside it.

original.note: Latin: late have I loved you. from Confessions 10.27: sero te amavi, pulchritudo tam antiqua et tam nova.

trapdoor: what you thought: late have I loved you is a sad regret.
what it means: God was within all along while Augustine searched outside, and now he answers.
what a scholar hears: five senses in a row, called, flashed, breathed, tasted, touched, each one answered in him: deafness broken, blindness scattered, breath drawn, hunger, burning.
guess: Augustine's cry: God was within while he looked outside
a song Augustine wrote for his mother's funeral
a regret that he started his book too late
recall: we touched it for a moment

chat.says: gave the testimony. said i don't have a moment, just slow. a 7th grader asked 'so you were late?' lol
options: Augustine said late too. God was within the whole time; late isn't too late.
Say no, you were right on time. Admitting you were slow sounds weak.
Say yes, and that late believers count a little less than early ones.
chat.meaning: Augustine: late have I loved you; you were within, and I was outside. Late love is still love, spoken to God.
